svg.title: Two Pointers and Sliding Window: Search-Space Elimination and Monotonicity
svg.desc: Animated step-by-step visualization of opposite-direction two pointers eliminating pairs on a sorted array to find target 18 in O(n) time, paired with a sliding window expanding R and shrinking L monotonically to maintain sum at most 10.
svg.text: Two Pointers & Sliding Window: Search-Space Elimination & Monotonicity
Opposite-Direction O(n) Pair Elimination (Two Sum II) vs Monotonic [L, R) Window Contraction

g.text: All pairs (k, 5) with k >= 0 exceed 18 -> eliminate 28 (right--)
All pairs (k, 4) with k >= 0 exceed 18 -> eliminate 19 (right--)
All pairs (0, k) with k <= 3 are under 18 -> eliminate 2 (left++)
All pairs (k, 3) with k >= 1 exceed 18 -> eliminate 15 (right--)
Converged in 5 steps (at most n - 1 steps total) with O(1) space

svg.text: Why O(n) Holds: Geometric Row/Column Elimination
Each comparison discards an entire row or column of the n x n pair space in O(1):

g.text: All k >= L: A[k] + A[R] > T
All k <= R: A[L] + A[k] < T
Distance (R - L) drops by 1 per step

svg.text: 3-Step Monotonic Loop (Total moves of L + R <= 2n):
Neither L nor R ever moves backward: each element enters once and exits at most once.
Sliding Window FAILS when negative numbers exist!
Adding A[R] < 0 can decrease sum; removing A[L] < 0 can increase sum.
Monotonicity breaks -> shrinking L might miss valid subarrays ahead.
Fix for "Subarray Sum = K" with negatives: Prefix Sum + Hash Map
Invariant guarantee: Opposite-direction eliminates O(n) candidates per step; Sliding Window bounds L and R to <= 2n increments total.
